newsitem.title: UK: DMG looks for new chairman as Craven retires.
newsitem.headline: DMG looks for new chairman as Craven retires.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the investment banking arm of Germany's Deutsche Bank AG , said Tuesday its chairman Sir John Craven would retire but it has not yet singled out his successor.
The firm, which has been plagued by problems in its fund management arm, stressed Craven's departure was not related to difficulties in that area.
A DMG spokesman said Craven would retire at the end of May but would join the advisory board of the Deutsche Bank group. He declined to comment on who might succeed Craven.
"That will be decided in due course," he said, adding that Craven "continues to be a close friend and colleague of the Deutsche Bank group."
Craven, 56, was chief executive of Morgan Grenfell from 1987 to 1989 when he was made chairman of the group. Before that he founded mergers and acquisitions boutique Phoenix Securities.
He was previously deputy chairman of British merchant bank SG Warburg, which he joined in 1967.
Craven was knighted last year and earlier this month was appointed as the new chairman of British conglomerate Lonrho Plc, a position he takes over from John Leahy on Wednesday.
